<content>
# EchoGuard

Privacy-preserving, camera-free motion and potential-fall sensing with Wi-Fi
Channel State Information (CSI) from two ESP32 boards.

> **Disclaimer.** EchoGuard is a hackathon research prototype. It is **not a
> medical device**, is **not medically validated**, and must not be relied on
> to detect falls or summon help. No accuracy claims are made.

## Status

| Milestone | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. CSI connection: firmware, serial parser, recorder, CLI monitor | implemented |
| 2. Live dashboard: signal processing, motion score, local web UI | implemented |
| 3. Calibration and labeled recording | implemented |
| 4. Heuristic fall detection | planned |
| 5. Simulation, replay polish, export | planned |

**Not verified yet:** the firmware has not been compiled (ESP-IDF was not
installed on the development machine) and no ESP32 was connected, so the
hardware path (flash, CSI capture, serial streaming) has **not** been tested
end to end. The Python side is tested against the documented Espressif format
using format fixtures (`tests/fixtures/`, not real captures). The dashboard
was exercised by replaying those fixtures and with generated test signals;
the motion score thresholds have not been tuned on real CSI yet. Calibration
and labeled recording were tested with generated signals and fixture replays
only; no calibration from a real room exists yet.

## Architecture

```
 ESP32 #1 (transmitter)            ESP32 #2 (receiver)              MacBook
 firmware/transmitter     ESP-NOW  firmware/receiver      USB       backend/
 broadcast 100 Hz  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~> CSI callback -> queue  ======>   parser -> buffer
 ch 11, HT40, MCS0                 printer task: CSI_DATA  serial   -> recorder / CLI
 MAC 1a:00:00:00:00:00             lines at 921600 baud             -> processing -> dashboard
```

* Two ESP32s only. No router, no mesh, no internet at runtime.
* The receiver prints the official esp-csi `CSI_DATA` CSV format, so the
  official Espressif tools also work with it.
* A Raspberry Pi can replace the Mac as host (same Python code), but is not required.

## Repository layout

```
firmware/transmitter/   ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_send)
firmware/receiver/      ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_recv)
firmware/flash_helper.sh  guarded build+flash helper (explicit port + confirmation)
backend/                csi_parser, sources (serial/replay), ports, buffer, recorder, cli,
                        config, processing, activity, engine, calibration, recording
dashboard/              Flask server (server.py, __main__.py) + static/ offline UI (HTML/CSS/JS)
tests/                  pytest suite + format fixtures
data/                   config.json, recordings/, calibration/, exports/, models/ (gitignored)
```

## macOS setup (host software)

```bash
brew install python@3.11        # if /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11 is missing
make setup                      # creates .venv and installs pinned requirements.txt
make test                       # runs the unit tests
```

`make setup` prefers Python 3.11 (falls back to 3.12). Python 3.14 is avoided
because binary wheels for some pinned packages may not exist yet. Internet is
only needed for this install step.

No internet? If a local interpreter already has the packages from
`requirements.txt` (numpy, scipy, pandas, pyserial, flask, pytest), build the
venv on top of it without any download:

```bash
make setup-offline                                   # default: ~/miniconda3/bin/python3.12
make setup-offline PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP=/path/to/python3 # any other interpreter
```

This recreates `.venv` with `--system-site-packages` and checks the imports.
Optional ML extras (scikit-learn, joblib, used later for Random Forest
training) are in `requirements-ml.txt`: `make setup-ml`.

## ESP-IDF installation (macOS)

```bash
brew install cmake ninja dfu-util ccache
mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp
git clone -b v5.5.1 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git
cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32,esp32s3,esp32c3,esp32c6
. ./export.sh                    # run in every new terminal (or add an alias)
idf.py --version
```

See the [ESP-IDF get-started guide](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/get-started/index.html)
for details. The first receiver build downloads the `esp_csi_gain_ctrl`
component (needs internet once).

## Identify your boards (read-only)

```bash
make ports                                   # lists ports, flags likely ESP32s
esptool.py --port /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX chip_id   # prints chip type + MAC, writes nothing
```

`chip_id` resets the board but does not write flash. **Do not connect the third
ESP32 that holds firmware you want to keep**; if it is plugged in, unplug it
before flashing anything. Nothing in this repository flashes automatically.

## Build and flash

Pick the target that `chip_id` reported (`esp32`, `esp32s3`, `esp32c3`, `esp32c6`).

Receiver (CSI source, connected to the Mac):

```bash
. ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
cd firmware/receiver
idf.py set-target esp32s3                    # use your chip
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-XXXX flash monitor
```

Transmitter (can be powered by any USB supply once flashed):

```bash
cd firmware/transmitter
idf.py set-target esp32                      # use your chip
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY flash monitor
```

Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3 (and other boards with only native USB): add the
USB-Serial-JTAG console overlay, otherwise no serial output appears:

```bash
idf.py -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag" set-target esp32s3
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor
```

Guarded alternative (read-only chip check, target match, typed confirmation):

```bash
firmware/flash_helper.sh --port /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX --role rx --target esp32s3 --usbjtag
firmware/flash_helper.sh --port /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY --role tx --target esp32
```

More details and all Kconfig options: [firmware/README.md](firmware/README.md).

## Milestone 1 usage

Close `idf.py monitor` first (`Ctrl-]`), then:

```bash
make ports
make monitor                      # PORT=auto; or: make monitor PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --port auto --record data/recordings/test.csv
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --replay data/recordings/test.csv
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --replay tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt --duration 3
```

Once per second the monitor prints connection state, total CSI packets, packet
rate, malformed lines, sequence gaps, RSSI (mean/std), noise floor, CSI length,
chip family, mean amplitude and a sparkline of the 52 valid LLTF subcarrier
amplitudes, plus the device's own `EG_RX_STATS`. Before any packet arrives it
prints `waiting for CSI packets` (no values are invented). Walk between the
boards and the sparkline / mean amplitude should change.

`--port auto` picks the single likely ESP32 port; if several are connected it
listens (read-only) on each for `CSI_DATA` and picks the one that emits it.
The serial source reconnects automatically after unplugging.

Recordings are CSV files with `host_ts_iso,host_ts_unix,raw_line`; replay feeds
the raw lines through the same parser. Raw `idf.py monitor` logs (`.txt`/`.log`)
can be replayed too (at 100 lines/s, since they have no host timestamps).

## Milestone 2: live dashboard

```bash
make dashboard                                   # http://127.0.0.1:8050/ opens in the browser
make dashboard ARGS="--serial auto"              # start reading the receiver right away
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --serial /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --replay data/recordings/test.csv --speed 1 --loop
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --no-browser --port 8599 --replay tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt
```

In the page, the **Data source** card selects a serial port (`auto` or a
listed `/dev/cu.*` device, baud 921600) or a replay file (recordings under
`data/` and the format fixtures), with speed and loop options. Close
`idf.py monitor` first; only one program can open the port.

Panels:

* **Connection status**: source state, port, reconnects and last error;
  packet rate and counts; RSSI (last, mean, sd), noise floor and mean CSI
  amplitude; malformed lines (by reason), sequence gaps and duplicates;
  a signal-quality badge with the reasons when data is insufficient; the TX/RX
  configuration seen in the packets (chip family, channel, secondary channel,
  bandwidth, CSI length, subcarrier count, TX MAC) and the device's own
  `EG_RX_STATS` / `EG_TX_STATS`.
* **Motion classification**: one of *Empty room / low activity*, *Movement
  detected*, *Rapid movement*, *Potential fall* (set by the fall detector in
  Milestone 4) or *Unknown / insufficient data*, plus the current motion
  score, baseline deviation and thresholds.
* **Live CSI**: scrolling heatmap of the normalised subcarrier amplitudes
  (time left to right, newest at right, with colour scale), mean amplitude,
  motion activity score with the movement / rapid threshold lines, baseline
  deviation, and RSSI over the last 30 s.

A **REPLAY of recorded data** banner is shown during replays (a
**SIMULATED DATA** banner is reserved for the simulation mode). Before data
arrives every field shows `No data yet` / `-`; nothing is invented.

Signal processing (`backend/processing.py`), per packet: the 52 valid LLTF
subcarrier amplitudes (C5/C6: all non-zero subcarriers) are divided by their
mean (removes AGC gain jumps), a Hampel filter replaces impulsive outliers per
subcarrier, and an EMA smooths them. Over a 1 s window it computes the
temporal **variance** (mean per-subcarrier std), the **diff energy** (RMS of
the first difference), the **baseline deviation** (mean z-score of the window
profile against the calibration baseline, or against a slow 30 s adaptive
reference until a calibration exists) and the **motion score**
`0.5 * (variance / noise_var + diff_energy / noise_diff)`; with a calibration
an empty room scores about 1. Data quality is *insufficient* (activity
*Unknown*) when the packet rate is below 20 Hz, the window is less than 70%
covered, the CSI layout changed, or no packet arrived for 1 s. Parameters and
thresholds live in `data/config.json` (created with defaults on first start).
**Until calibration (Milestone 3) the thresholds are uncalibrated defaults**,
so the classification is only indicative.

Framework choice: the dashboard is a small Flask app with a self-contained
HTML/CSS/vanilla-JavaScript page that draws its charts on `<canvas>`. It needs
no CDN or internet (Streamlit/Plotly could not be installed offline and are
not required). The page polls `/api/status`, `/api/series` and `/api/heatmap`
about 2.5 times per second.

**Security note:** the dashboard has **no authentication**. It binds to
`127.0.0.1` by default. `--host 0.0.0.0` (e.g. to view it from another
machine, or on a Raspberry Pi host) prints a warning: anyone who can reach the
address can see the data and change the data source. Only do that on a
trusted network.

## Milestone 3: calibration and labeled recording

### Self-calibration

Open the **Calibration** tab after starting the data source (live serial, or a
replay at 1x). Enter a placement name (e.g. `living-room`), adjust the step
durations if needed and click **Start calibration**. Each step starts after a
lead-in countdown (default 5 s, so you can leave the room) and records for its
duration of packet time:

1. **Empty room baseline** (15-30 s, default 20 s): nobody in the room, nothing moving.
2. **Walking** (default 15 s): walk back and forth across the line between the boards.
3. **Standing still** (default 10 s): stand in the sensing area without moving.
4. **Ordinary sitting** (default 10 s): sit down on a chair as usual and stay seated.

The first second of each step is skipped (the 1 s analysis window still holds
data from before the step). A progress bar, the live data-quality badge and
the per-step frame counts are shown; any step can be redone or cancelled. A
step fails, and must be redone, when fewer than 80% of its frames had
sufficient data quality (packet rate >= 20 Hz, window coverage, stable CSI
layout) or the sensor configuration changed. After the last step EchoGuard
computes:

* the empty-room **baseline profile** (per-subcarrier mean and std of the
  normalised, filtered amplitudes) used for the baseline deviation,
* **noise levels** (median and p95 of variance, diff energy, deviation and
  score in the empty room); the medians become the motion-score normalisation,
  so a calibrated empty room scores about 1,
* per-step distributions of the calibrated motion score, shown as a box plot
  together with the empty-room profile (mean +/- std band) vs the walking
  profile,
* **preliminary thresholds**: `quiet = max(p95 empty, p95 standing)`;
  `low = quiet + 0.25 (walking median - quiet)`, `movement = quiet + 0.5
  (walking median - quiet)`, `rapid = max(1.5 walking p95, 2 movement)`, kept
  in increasing order. If walking is not at least 1.5x above the quiet p95 the
  steps are reported as not separable and conservative fallback thresholds
  are used, with a warning.

**Save calibration** writes `data/calibration/<sensor_key>.json` and applies
it immediately. The key combines the placement and the sensor configuration
seen in the packets, e.g. `living-room__classic_1a0000000000_ch11-2_len128`
(chip family, TX MAC, channel, secondary channel, CSI length). When the
dashboard later sees that configuration, it loads the newest matching
calibration automatically (preferring the last used placement); if the
active calibration does not match a newly detected configuration it is
dropped. Saved calibrations can be listed, loaded, deleted (with
confirmation) or switched off (**Use uncalibrated**); **Recalibrate** starts
the wizard again. The active calibration is shown in the top bar and in the
TX/RX configuration card. Calibrations computed from simulated data are marked
`synthetic: true` (key suffix `__synthetic`) and are never applied to real
data. The thresholds are heuristics from one run, not validated limits.

### Labeled recording

In the **Record** tab create a session (placement name and notes) or select an
existing one, choose an optional fixed duration and pre-countdown, then click
a label: *Empty room*, *Standing still*, *Walking*, *Sitting*, *Lying down*,
*Rapid sitting* or *Simulated fall*. The take timer and packet count update
live; click the active label or **Stop take** to end it. Takes can be deleted
(with confirmation). Recording is disabled while a live serial source is
disconnected, and real and synthetic data are never mixed in one session.
Every raw serial line is written by the engine thread, so nothing depends on
the UI refresh.

File layout:

```
data/recordings/<session_id>/session.json
data/recordings/<session_id>/<take_index>_<label>_<start_ts>.csv   e.g. 001_walking_20250101T120000.csv
data/calibration/<sensor_key>.json
```

`session_id` is `YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-<placement>`. `session.json` contains the
creation time, sensor configuration, source kind, synthetic flag, notes, app
version and a `takes` index (label, start/end, duration, packet and line
counts, stop reason). Take CSV columns: `host_ts_iso, host_ts_unix,
session_id, take_id, label, raw_line, rssi, id, channel, len,
local_timestamp`. The raw line is kept so a replay goes through the same
parser and pipeline.

### Replay of recordings

The **Replay recording** picker lists whole sessions (all takes in order, with
a 0.5 s pause between takes), single takes, other recordings and the format
fixtures, at 0.5x/1x/2x/5x or as fast as possible. During the replay of a
labeled take the banner and the motion card show the take label as **ground
truth**. Features are computed on replay time, so use 1x (or "as fast as
possible", which keeps the original timestamps) when comparing with live
behaviour; 2x/5x compress time and raise the motion score. From the command
line: `.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --replay data/recordings/<session_id>`.

### Machine-learning evaluation

Organise data collection as several sessions (different days, placements or
people). Any future classifier must be evaluated by **holding out complete
sessions** (e.g. leave-one-session-out). Random splits of packets or windows
from the same session leak information between training and test data and
give meaningless accuracy numbers. Synthetic sessions are not evidence of
real-world accuracy.

## Serial format

Receiver lines follow the official esp-csi format.

Classic ESP32 / ESP32-S3 / ESP32-C3 (25 fields):

```
type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data
CSI_DATA,0,94:d9:b3:80:8c:81,-30,11,1,6,1,0,1,0,1,0,0,-93,0,13,2,2751923,0,67,0,128,1,"[67,48,4,0,...]"
```

ESP32-C5 / ESP32-C6 (15 fields):

```
type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data
```

* `id` / `seq`: transmitter packet counter (used for loss / gap counting).
* `local_timestamp`: receiver clock in microseconds.
* `len`: number of integers in `data`. With `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY` (default on
  classic chips) it is 128.
* `first_word`: 1 means the first 4 values (subcarriers 0 and 1) are invalid.
* `data`: interleaved `[imag, real]` per subcarrier; decoded as
  `complex(raw[2k+1], raw[2k])` like the official parser. On classic chips the
  first 64 subcarriers are the LLTF in order 0..31, -32..-1; the 52 valid ones
  are indices 1..26 and 38..63.

EchoGuard additions (one line per second):

```
EG_RX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<csi_rx_total>,<csi_rx_rate_hz>,<queue_drops>,<seq_gaps>,<last_rssi>
EG_TX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<sent_ok>,<send_fail>,<rate_hz>
```

## Serial troubleshooting

* **Port names on macOS.** Native USB (XIAO ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3/C6/S3 USB
  port): `/dev/cu.usbmodem*`. USB-UART bridges: `/dev/cu.usbserial-*`,
  `/dev/cu.SLAB_USBtoUART` (CP210x), `/dev/cu.wchusbserial*` (CH34x). Use
  `/dev/cu.*`, not `/dev/tty.*`. `Bluetooth-Incoming-Port` and `debug-console`
  are macOS system ports, never an ESP32.
* **No port appears.** Try another cable (many are charge-only) and another USB
  port/hub. Recent macOS includes CP210x and CH34x drivers; for older systems
  install the vendor driver (Silicon Labs CP210x VCP, WCH CH34x).
* **Cannot connect / download mode.** Hold BOOT, tap RESET (or plug in while
  holding BOOT), then flash. Native-USB boards may re-enumerate under a new
  `usbmodem` name after flashing; re-run `make ports`.
* **Port busy.** Only one program can open a port. Close `idf.py monitor`
  (`Ctrl-]`), the Arduino serial monitor, `screen`, or another EchoGuard
  monitor.
* **Garbage characters.** The receiver UART runs at **921600** baud (`--baud
  921600`, the default). The transmitter uses the ESP-IDF default 115200.
* **No output on XIAO ESP32-S3.** The default config prints to UART0 pins, not
  the USB-C port. Rebuild with `sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag` (see above).
* **`waiting for CSI packets` but RX stats show 0 Hz.** Check that the
  transmitter is powered and both use the same channel (`ECHOGUARD_*_CHANNEL`).
* **High `queue_drops` or malformed lines.** The serial link is saturated:
  keep `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY=y`, or lower `ECHOGUARD_TX_RATE_HZ`.

## Tests

```bash
make test
```

Covers parsing of the documented official example lines (both variants),
complex decoding order, LLTF subcarrier selection and masking, malformed line
handling, stats lines, the bounded buffer (rate, sequence gaps with
wraparound), record/replay round trip, serial reconnect (fake serial and
pyserial `loop://`) and port classification. Milestone 2 adds signal
processing (constant vs. perturbed generated streams, Hampel spike
suppression, quality gates, layout changes, NaN masking, calibrated
normalisation), activity mapping, the engine (fixture replay, error handling,
no fabricated values without a source) and the dashboard API (Flask test
client, including rejection of path traversal and invalid ports). Milestone 3
adds calibration (ordered thresholds from separable generated streams,
fallback warning for inseparable data, refusal on insufficient quality,
redo/cancel, save/load round trip, sensor-key matching, auto-load, synthetic
calibrations never applied to real data), recording (exact labels, session
layout, take CSV columns, session.json takes index, duration/source-change
stops, replay of a recorded take reproducing the same parsed packets, whole
session replay with ground truth) and the new API routes (happy paths plus
invalid labels, placements, keys and path traversal rejected with 400). Test
signals are generated in the tests and are not real measurements.

args.text:
# EchoGuard

Camera-free motion and potential-fall sensing with Wi-Fi Channel State
Information (CSI) from two ESP32 boards. EchoGuard keeps your privacy because
it never uses a camera.

> **Disclaimer.** EchoGuard is a hackathon research prototype. It is **not a
> medical device**, is **not medically validated**, and must not be relied on
> to detect falls or summon help. No accuracy claims are made: the heuristic and the
> optional classifier have not been evaluated on held-out real recordings.

## Status

| Milestone | State |
| --- | --- |
| 1. CSI connection: firmware, serial parser, recorder, CLI monitor | implemented (firmware not compiled, see below) |
| 2. Live dashboard: signal processing, motion score, local web UI | implemented |
| 3. Calibration and labeled recording, replay | implemented |
| 4. Heuristic fall detection, alerts, event log, `evaluate` CLI | implemented |
| 5. Simulation mode, export, optional Random Forest training | implemented |

**Hardware integration and firmware compilation were NOT verified here.**
ESP-IDF was not installed on the development machine and no ESP32 was
connected, so flashing, CSI capture and serial streaming have not been tested
end to end. Everything on the Python side was tested against the documented
Espressif format (format fixtures, generated signals and the simulator). See
[Verification status](#verification-status).

## Architecture

```
 ESP32 #1 (transmitter)            ESP32 #2 (receiver)              MacBook (or Raspberry Pi)
 firmware/transmitter     ESP-NOW  firmware/receiver      USB       backend/
 broadcast 100 Hz  ~~~~~~~~~~~~~~> CSI callback -> queue  ======>   parser -> buffer -> recorder
 ch 11, HT40, MCS0                 printer task: CSI_DATA  serial   -> processing (motion score)
 MAC 1a:00:00:00:00:00             lines at 921600 baud             -> activity + fall heuristic
                                                                    -> alerts / event log
                                                                    -> dashboard (Flask, 127.0.0.1)
 simulation/ (SYNTHETIC CSI_DATA lines, MAC 02:51:4d:00:00:00) ---> same parser and pipeline
```

* You need only two ESP32s. There is no router, no mesh and no internet at runtime.
* The receiver prints the official esp-csi `CSI_DATA` CSV format, so the
  official Espressif tools also work with it.
* Live serial data, replays of recordings and the simulator all produce text
  lines that go through the same parser, processing, detector and dashboard.
* A Raspberry Pi can replace the Mac as host. It is optional.

## Quick start

```bash
make setup            # or, without internet: make setup-offline
make test
make dashboard-sim    # SYNTHETIC demo, no hardware: http://127.0.0.1:8050/
make dashboard        # real hardware: pick the serial port in the page (or ARGS="--serial auto")
```

## Repository layout

```
firmware/transmitter/     ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_send)
firmware/receiver/        ESP-IDF project (from esp-csi csi_recv)
firmware/flash_helper.sh  guarded build+flash helper (explicit port + confirmation)
backend/                  csi_parser, sources (serial/replay), ports, buffer, recorder, cli,
                          config, processing, activity, engine, calibration, recording,
                          detector (fall heuristic), alerts (alerts + event log), monitor (wiring),
                          offline (offline replay), export (CSV), ml/train_rf (optional)
dashboard/                Flask server (server.py, __main__.py) + static/ offline UI (HTML/CSS/JS)
simulation/               synthetic CSI generator (SimulationSource)
tests/                    pytest suite + format fixtures
data/                     config.json, events.jsonl, recordings/, calibration/, exports/, models/ (gitignored)
```

## macOS setup (host software)

```bash
brew install python@3.11        # if /opt/homebrew/bin/python3.11 is missing
make setup                      # creates .venv and installs pinned requirements.txt
make test                       # runs the unit tests
```

`make setup` prefers Python 3.11 and falls back to 3.12. Python 3.14 is avoided
because binary wheels for some pinned packages may not exist yet. You need internet
only for this install step.

If you have no internet but a local interpreter already has the packages from
`requirements.txt` (numpy, scipy, pandas, pyserial, flask, pytest), build the
venv on top of it without any download:

```bash
make setup-offline                                   # default: ~/miniconda3/bin/python3.12
make setup-offline PYTHON_BOOTSTRAP=/path/to/python3 # any other interpreter
```

Optional ML extras (scikit-learn, joblib) for Random Forest training:
`make setup-ml` (pip install -r requirements-ml.txt).

## ESP-IDF installation (macOS)

```bash
brew install cmake ninja dfu-util ccache
mkdir -p ~/esp && cd ~/esp
git clone -b v5.5.1 --recursive https://github.com/espressif/esp-idf.git
cd esp-idf && ./install.sh esp32,esp32s3,esp32c3,esp32c6
. ./export.sh                    # run in every new terminal (or add an alias)
idf.py --version
```

See the [ESP-IDF get-started guide](https://docs.espressif.com/projects/esp-idf/en/stable/esp32/get-started/index.html)
for details. The first receiver build downloads the `esp_csi_gain_ctrl`
component, which needs internet once.

## Two-board flashing procedure

Nothing in this repository flashes automatically. Flash exactly two boards,
one at a time:

1. **Unplug the third ESP32** (the one with firmware you want to keep). Never
   connect it while flashing.
2. Plug in the board that will be the **transmitter** only, then identify it
   (read-only):

   ```bash
   make ports                                       # lists ports, flags likely ESP32s
   esptool.py --port /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY chip_id # chip type + MAC, writes nothing
   ```

   `chip_id` resets the board but writes no flash. Note the chip type
   (`esp32`, `esp32s3`, `esp32c3`, `esp32c6`).
3. Build and flash the transmitter:

   ```bash
   . ~/esp/esp-idf/export.sh
   cd firmware/transmitter
   idf.py set-target esp32                      # the chip from step 2
   idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY flash monitor
   ```

   It prints a banner (target, channel, rate, MAC `1a:00:00:00:00:00`) and an
   `EG_TX_STATS` line every second. Unplug it and power it from any USB supply.
4. Plug in the **receiver** board only, identify it the same way, then:

   ```bash
   cd firmware/receiver
   idf.py set-target esp32s3                    # the chip from chip_id
   idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor
   ```

   You should see `CSI_DATA` lines and `EG_RX_STATS` once per second. Close
   the monitor with `Ctrl-]` before starting EchoGuard.

**Seeed Studio XIAO ESP32-S3** (and other boards that have only native USB): add the
USB-Serial-JTAG console overlay. Without it, no serial output appears:

```bash
idf.py -D SDKCONFIG_DEFAULTS="sdkconfig.defaults;sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag" set-target esp32s3
idf.py -p /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX flash monitor
```

Guarded alternative (read-only chip check, target match, typed confirmation):

```bash
firmware/flash_helper.sh --port /dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX --role rx --target esp32s3 --usbjtag
firmware/flash_helper.sh --port /dev/cu.usbserial-YYYY --role tx --target esp32
```

Both boards must use the same channel (default 11, `idf.py menuconfig` ->
EchoGuard options). More details and all Kconfig options:
[firmware/README.md](firmware/README.md).

## CLI monitor (Milestone 1)

```bash
make monitor                      # PORT=auto; or: make monitor PORT=/dev/cu.usbmodemXXXX
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --port auto --record data/recordings/test.csv
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --replay tests/fixtures/classic_esp32s3_sample.txt --duration 3
make simulate SCENARIO=potential_fall DURATION=12      # SYNTHETIC data
```

Once per second the monitor prints the connection state, packet counts and
rate, malformed lines, sequence gaps, RSSI, noise floor, CSI length, mean
amplitude, a sparkline of the 52 valid LLTF subcarriers and the device's
`EG_RX_STATS`. It also prints the motion score, the activity, the data
quality and the fall-detector state. A potential-fall event is printed with every
criterion. Before any packet arrives it prints `waiting for CSI packets`
(no values are invented). `--port auto` picks the single likely ESP32 port. If
several are connected, it listens read-only on each for `CSI_DATA`. The serial
source reconnects automatically after unplugging.

## Dashboard guide

```bash
make dashboard                                   # http://127.0.0.1:8050/ opens in the browser
make dashboard ARGS="--serial auto"              # start reading the receiver right away
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --replay data/recordings/<session_id> --speed 1
.venv/bin/python -m dashboard --simulate demo    # SYNTHETIC data
```

* **Data source** tabs: *Live serial* (port `auto` or a `/dev/cu.*` device,
  baud 921600), *Replay recording* (sessions, takes, other recordings,
  fixtures; 0.5x to 5x or as fast as possible; loop), *Simulation*,
  *Calibration* and *Record*.
* **Connection status**: source state, port, reconnects, last error; packet
  rate; RSSI, noise floor, mean amplitude; malformed lines and sequence gaps; a
  signal-quality badge with reasons; the TX/RX configuration seen in the
  packets and the device stats lines.
* **Motion classification**: *Empty room / low activity*, *Movement
  detected*, *Rapid movement*, *Potential fall* (while an alert is unresolved)
  or *Unknown / insufficient data*, with the motion score, baseline deviation,
  variance, diff energy, thresholds and the replay ground truth.
* **Potential-fall alerts**: the alert card (countdown progress bar, the
  criteria table, the **Cancel alert** button, the simulated caregiver message
  after the countdown), the detector state, editable heuristic settings and the
  event log.
* **Live CSI**: scrolling subcarrier heatmap, mean amplitude, motion score
  (with stillness / movement / rapid lines), baseline deviation, RSSI.
* **Export**: CSV downloads of the current buffer or a recording.

Banners: **REPLAY of recorded data** during replays and **SIMULATED DATA -
synthetic, not evidence of real-world accuracy** whenever the source is the
simulator or a recording made from it. The footer always shows the medical
disclaimer.

Framework choice: the dashboard uses Flask with a self-contained
HTML/CSS/vanilla-JavaScript page that draws its charts on `<canvas>`, instead of
Streamlit, because Streamlit (and Plotly) could not be installed offline
here. It needs no CDN and no internet. The page polls the JSON API about 2.5 times per
second.

**Security note:** the dashboard has **no authentication**. It binds to
`127.0.0.1` by default. `--host 0.0.0.0` prints a warning: anyone who can reach
the address can see the data, change the source, cancel alerts and export
recordings. Use it only on a trusted network.

### Signal processing

Per packet (`backend/processing.py`), the 52 valid LLTF subcarrier amplitudes
(C5/C6: all non-zero subcarriers) go through three steps:

1. They are divided by their mean, which removes AGC gain jumps.
2. A Hampel filter replaces impulsive outliers.
3. An EMA smooths them.

Over a 1 s window the processor then computes:

* the **variance** (mean per-subcarrier std),
* the **diff energy** (RMS of the first difference),
* the **baseline deviation** (z-score against the calibration baseline, or
  against a slow adaptive reference),
* the **motion score** `0.5 * (variance / noise_var + diff_energy / noise_diff)`.
  A calibrated empty room scores about 1.

Data quality is *insufficient* when any of these is true:

* the packet rate is below 20 Hz,
* the window is less than 70% covered,
* the CSI layout changed,
* no packet arrived for 1 s.

Settings live in `data/config.json`, which is created with defaults on first
start. The uncalibrated thresholds are low 1.5, movement 2.5 and rapid 6.0.

## Calibration

Start the source, open **Calibration**, enter a placement name and click
**Start calibration**. Each step has a lead-in countdown and records for its
duration (packet time):

1. **Empty room baseline** (15-30 s, default 20 s)
2. **Walking** across the sensing area (default 15 s)
3. **Standing still** (default 10 s)
4. **Ordinary sitting** (default 10 s)

Each step can be redone or cancelled. A step fails if fewer than 80% of its
frames had sufficient quality. The result shows a box plot of the motion score
per step and the baseline profile (mean +/- std) against walking. It contains:

* the empty-room baseline profile,
* the noise levels, which normalise the score,
* preliminary thresholds: `quiet = max(p95 empty, p95 standing)`,
  `low = quiet + 0.25 gap`, `movement = quiet + 0.5 gap`,
  `rapid = max(1.5 walking p95, 2 movement)`, where gap is the walking median
  minus quiet. Fallback values and a warning are used if walking is not
  separable from the quiet steps.

**Save calibration** writes `data/calibration/<placement>__<chip>_<txmac>_ch<ch>-<sec>_len<len>.json`.
That calibration loads automatically whenever the same sensor configuration
is seen again. You can also list, load, delete (with confirmation), clear or
recalibrate. Simulated calibrations carry `synthetic: true`, get a
`__synthetic` key suffix and are never applied to real data.

## Recording and replay

In **Record**, create a session (placement and notes) or select one. Then click
one of the labels: *Empty room*, *Standing still*, *Walking*, *Sitting*,
*Lying down*, *Rapid sitting*, *Simulated fall*. You can set a fixed duration
and a pre-countdown. The engine thread writes every raw line:

```
data/recordings/<YYYYMMDD-HHMMSS-placement>/session.json
data/recordings/<session_id>/<take_index>_<label>_<start_ts>.csv
```

Take CSV columns are `host_ts_iso, host_ts_unix, session_id, take_id, label,
raw_line, rssi, id, channel, len, local_timestamp`. `session.json` holds the
sensor configuration, source kind, `synthetic` flag, notes and a takes index.
A session never mixes real and synthetic data. Recording is disabled while a
live serial source is disconnected.

Replay a whole session (takes in order) or one take from the **Replay** tab
or with `--replay`. The take label appears as ground truth. Use 1x, or "as fast
as possible" (which keeps the original timestamps), to compare with live behaviour.

## Fall heuristic (Milestone 4)

`backend/detector.py` evaluates every motion frame (10 Hz, data time) against
three explainable, configurable criteria:

1. **Sudden motion spike.** The motion score reaches the spike threshold
   (default: the active `rapid` threshold) and rose by at least
   `min_rise_fraction` x spike (default 0.5) within the previous
   `rise_window_s` (1.5 s). Sustained vigorous activity is not "sudden".
2. **Post-event stillness.** After the last spike frame, the score must drop
   to the stillness threshold (default: the `low` threshold) within
   `max_gap_s` (2 s). It must then stay at or below that threshold for
   `stillness_duration_s` (3 s).
3. **Data quality.** Every frame from the start of the rise window to the
   decision must be quality-ok (no *Unknown* frames) with at least
   `min_packet_rate_hz` (20 Hz). Any bad frame aborts the candidate.

Stillness is evaluated **only after a spike**. Low movement alone never
raises an alert, because an empty room or a person sitting still is not a fall. After a
detection a `refractory_s` (30 s) period suppresses repeats. Each event lists
all criteria with value, rule and pass/fail (`motion_spike`, `sudden_rise`,
`stillness_onset`, `stillness_level`, `stillness_duration`, `data_quality`,
`packet_rate`). The dashboard shows them in the alert card. The detector
card shows the current candidate and the last rejected candidate with its
reason.

**Alerts** (`backend/alerts.py`): an event starts an alert with a countdown
(default 30 s). The engine shows *Potential fall* until the alert is cancelled
or dismissed. If nobody cancels in time, a **simulated caregiver
notification** appears. It is only an event-log entry and a message in the UI:
nothing is sent and no network call is made. The event log keeps activity
changes (debounced 1 s), alerts, notifications, cancellations, calibrations,
recordings, exports and connection events. The newest 500 stay in memory and
every event is appended to `data/events.jsonl` (rotated to `.1` at 5 MB).

**Tuning.** Edit the *Heuristic settings* in the alert card. Changes are
saved to the `fall` / `alerts` sections of `data/config.json`. A spike or
stillness value of 0 means "derive from the motion thresholds", which are
calibrated after a calibration. Known limitations:

* A rapid sit followed by sitting still can trigger an alert.
* A real fall followed by continued movement may not trigger one.
* Noise above the stillness threshold prevents detection, so calibrate first.

Check the heuristic on your own labeled recordings:

```bash
.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli evaluate --session data/recordings/<session_id> [--calibration data/calibration/<key>.json] [--json]
make evaluate SESSION=data/recordings/<session_id>
```

It replays each take through the same processing and a fresh detector and
reports, per take, the label, packets, good-quality fraction, maximum motion
score and whether an alert fired (with criteria). It also prints a per-label
summary. This checks the heuristic on recorded examples. It is not an accuracy
estimate.

## Simulation mode (Milestone 5)

**Simulated data is synthetic. It must never be used as evidence of
real-world fall-detection accuracy.**

The *Simulation* tab (or `--simulate`, `make simulate`, `make dashboard-sim`)
offers these scenarios:

* `empty_room`
* `walking`
* `sitting` (sit down, sit, stand up)
* `rapid_movement`
* `potential_fall` (walking, a rapid burst, then lying still)
* `demo` (a scripted sequence of all of the above)

Sliders control the noise (0-0.5), motion strength (0-3), event duration
(0.2-10 s; it sets the fall-like burst, 3x for the rapid bout and 1.5x for the
sit-down transition) and packet rate (10-200 Hz; below 20 Hz the data quality is
insufficient by design).

The model has these parts:

* a static multipath profile,
* a few person-related scatterers whose path length follows the scenario,
* complex Gaussian noise,
* AGC gain jitter,
* int8 quantisation,
* 0.5% packet loss,
* an RSSI around -45 dBm.

It emits official classic `CSI_DATA` lines (len 128), so the same parser and
pipeline run. Simulated packets use the locally administered TX MAC
`02:51:4d:00:00:00`. The source kind is `simulation` with `synthetic: true` in
the dashboard snapshot, in recordings (`session.json`, takes), in
calibrations (`__synthetic` keys), in alerts and events, and in exports
(`synthetic` column, `_synthetic` file names). The current scenario phase is
shown as `... [simulated]`.

## Export

The **Export** card, `POST /api/export`, writes `data/exports/*.csv`:

* **current buffer**: up to 3000 packets with the frame features in effect,
* **recording**: a session or take, re-processed offline with the same pipeline.

Each row contains timestamps, source kind, the `synthetic` flag, session/take
and label, packet metadata, motion score, variance, diff energy, baseline
deviation, quality, activity, and `amp_lltf_<i>` amplitudes of the valid
subcarriers. Downloads are served only from `data/exports` and file names are validated.

## Optional Random Forest training

```bash
make setup-ml                                     # scikit-learn + joblib (needs internet once)
.venv/bin/python -m backend.ml.train_rf --recordings data/recordings
make train-rf ARGS="--folds 5 --trees 200"
```

`backend/ml/train_rf.py` replays every take through the live processing
pipeline. It extracts 2 s windows of quality-ok frames (mean/std/min/max of
the motion features, largest score rise, amplitude and RSSI variability)
labeled with the take label. It then evaluates a `RandomForestClassifier` with
**grouped folds by `session_id`**: whole sessions are held out
(leave-one-session-out with few sessions). Packets or windows are never split
randomly. Per-class precision/recall/F1 and the confusion matrix are computed
on held-out sessions only. A final model plus a JSON metadata file are saved
to `data/models/`.

Training is **refused** in these cases:

* fewer than 2 real sessions,
* any session is synthetic (`session.json` flag or simulator MAC), unless you
  pass `--allow-synthetic` (pipeline test only; every output and file name is
  then marked SYNTHETIC) or `--exclude-synthetic`.

Even with real data, the numbers describe only the recorded sessions, people
and placement. They are not a validated fall-detection accuracy. The model is
experimental and is not used by the dashboard. The module imports neither
flask nor pandas, so it also runs in a minimal numpy + scikit-learn Python.

## Offline operation

After installation nothing needs the internet. The firmware uses ESP-NOW
between the two boards, and the dashboard serves only local files (no CDN, no
external URLs; a strict Content-Security-Policy). The simulated notification
makes no network calls. Internet is needed only for `make setup` / `make
setup-ml` and for the first ESP-IDF build (component download).

## Optional Raspberry Pi host

The same Python app runs on a Raspberry Pi (64-bit Raspberry Pi OS, Python 3.11):

```bash
sudo apt install python3-venv python3-dev
sudo usermod -aG dialout $USER     # serial access; log out and back in
make setup && make test
make dashboard ARGS="--serial auto --no-browser"
```

The receiver appears as `/dev/ttyACM*` (native USB, e.g. XIAO ESP32-S3) or
`/dev/ttyUSB*` (CP210x/CH34x bridges). `--serial auto` finds it, or pass
`--serial /dev/ttyACM0`. To view the dashboard from another machine, use an SSH
tunnel (`ssh -L 8050:127.0.0.1:8050 pi@<host>`). Avoid `--host 0.0.0.0`,
because the dashboard has no authentication.

## Serial format

Classic ESP32 / ESP32-S3 / ESP32-C3 (25 fields):

```
type,id,mac,rssi,rate,sig_mode,mcs,bandwidth,smoothing,not_sounding,aggregation,stbc,fec_coding,sgi,noise_floor,ampdu_cnt,channel,secondary_channel,local_timestamp,ant,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data
CSI_DATA,0,94:d9:b3:80:8c:81,-30,11,1,6,1,0,1,0,1,0,0,-93,0,13,2,2751923,0,67,0,128,1,"[67,48,4,0,...]"
```

ESP32-C5 / ESP32-C6 (15 fields):

```
type,seq,mac,rssi,rate,noise_floor,fft_gain,agc_gain,channel,local_timestamp,sig_len,rx_state,len,first_word,data
```

* `id` / `seq`: transmitter packet counter (loss / gap counting).
* `local_timestamp`: receiver clock in microseconds.
* `len`: number of integers in `data` (128 with `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY`, the
  default on classic chips).
* `first_word`: 1 means subcarriers 0 and 1 are invalid.
* `data`: interleaved `[imag, real]`, decoded as `complex(raw[2k+1], raw[2k])`
  like the official parser. Classic LLTF order is 0..31, -32..-1. The 52 valid
  subcarriers are indices 1..26 and 38..63.

EchoGuard adds one line per second:

```
EG_RX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<csi_rx_total>,<csi_rx_rate_hz>,<queue_drops>,<seq_gaps>,<last_rssi>
EG_TX_STATS,<uptime_ms>,<sent_ok>,<send_fail>,<rate_hz>
```

## Serial troubleshooting

* **Port names on macOS.** Native USB (XIAO ESP32-S3, ESP32-C3/C6/S3 USB
  port) shows up as `/dev/cu.usbmodem*`. USB-UART bridges show up as
  `/dev/cu.usbserial-*`, `/dev/cu.SLAB_USBtoUART` (CP210x) or
  `/dev/cu.wchusbserial*` (CH34x). Use `/dev/cu.*`, not `/dev/tty.*`.
  `Bluetooth-Incoming-Port` and `debug-console` are macOS system ports, never
  an ESP32.
* **No port appears.** Try another cable (many are charge-only) or another USB
  port/hub. Recent macOS includes CP210x and CH34x drivers. On older systems,
  install the vendor driver.
* **Cannot connect / download mode.** Hold BOOT, tap RESET (or plug in while
  holding BOOT), then flash. Native-USB boards may re-enumerate under a new
  name. Re-run `make ports`.
* **Port busy.** Only one program can open a port. Close `idf.py monitor`
  (`Ctrl-]`), `screen`, the Arduino serial monitor or another EchoGuard
  instance.
* **Garbage characters.** The receiver runs at **921600** baud (the default).
  The transmitter uses 115200.
* **No output on XIAO ESP32-S3.** Rebuild with `sdkconfig.defaults.usbjtag`.
* **`waiting for CSI packets` and RX stats show 0 Hz.** Make sure the
  transmitter is powered and both boards use the same channel.
* **High `queue_drops` or malformed lines.** Keep `ECHOGUARD_RX_LLTF_ONLY=y`,
  or lower `ECHOGUARD_TX_RATE_HZ`.
* **Activity stays *Unknown*.** Check the quality reasons in the dashboard.
  The packet rate must be at least 20 Hz.

## Tests

```bash
make test
```

The suite uses format fixtures and generated test signals. None of it is real
measurement data. It covers:

* the parser (official example lines, both variants, decoding order, masking, malformed lines),
* the buffer, record/replay and serial reconnect,
* port classification,
* signal processing, activity mapping and the engine,
* calibration and recording,
* the fall detector:
  * a spike followed by stillness triggers, with all criteria reported,
  * a spike without stillness, stillness without a spike, or a late stillness does not trigger,
  * quality gating,
  * the refractory period,
  * configured and calibrated thresholds are respected,
* alerts (countdown, cancel, simulated notification) and event log persistence and rotation,
* the simulator:
  * its lines parse with the official parser,
  * it is marked synthetic,
  * end to end through the engine, `potential_fall` raises an alert and the other scenarios do not,
* RF tooling:
  * session-grouped splits never mix sessions,
  * training is refused for synthetic or single-session data,

FEAT-004 is done and marked "completed" in `features/FEAT-004.json`, with detailed findings recorded there. `make test` gives 216 passed and 2 skipped; the two skipped tests are the scikit-learn training tests, because `.venv` has no scikit-learn. Nothing was committed, `git add -N .` was run, and firmware C code was not touched.

**Verification**
- **Dashboard server** (temporary wrapper on port 8599): posting `{kind: 'simulation', scenario: 'potential_fall'}` produced an active alert after about 8.5 s. All 7 criteria passed, the countdown was running, activity was `potential_fall`, the source was marked synthetic and the TX MAC was `02:51:4d:00:00:00`.
  - `POST /api/alerts/cancel` changed the alert to cancelled and activity went straight back to `empty_low`.
  - The event log listed the source start, activity changes, the alert and the cancel.
  - Buffer export and download both worked.
- **CLI**: `.venv/bin/python -m backend.cli monitor --simulate potential_fall --duration 10` printed frames and a potential-fall event at +8.1 s with PASS/FAIL per criterion.
- **Random Forest training did run**, but under the `opencv_python` interpreter (sklearn 1.7.1), not `.venv`. That interpreter has no pandas, flask, pyserial or pytest, so it also confirms the training path doesn't need them.
  - Three generated synthetic sessions were refused without the flag (exit code 2).
  - With `--allow-synthetic` it ran 3 session-grouped folds, printed a report labelled SYNTHETIC, and saved and reloaded a `*_synthetic.joblib` file (in a temp dir).
- **UI checks**: `node --check` passes and there are no external URLs in `dashboard/static`. A temporary node script with a stubbed DOM ran `app.js` against real API data with an active alert; the alert card, countdown, 7 criteria rows, event log and synthetic banner rendered without errors.
- Temp scripts, `data/events.jsonl`, `data/config.json` and the export CSVs were deleted afterwards.

**What was built**
- **Detector** (`backend/detector.py`): a potential fall needs a sudden spike (score at the `rapid` threshold, rising quickly), then stillness starting within 2 s and lasting 3 s. Every frame in between must have good data quality. There is a 30 s refractory period, and stillness without a spike never fires.
- **Alerts and event log** (`backend/alerts.py`): 30 s countdown, cancel, then a simulated caregiver notification that sends nothing anywhere. Events are kept in memory and appended to `data/events.jsonl`.
- **Wiring** (`backend/monitor.py`): connects detector and alerts to the Engine, shows *Potential fall* while an alert is open, and adds `alert` and `detector` sections to `/api/status`.
- **Simulation** (`simulation/generator.py`): six scenarios (`empty_room`, `walking`, `sitting`, `rapid_movement`, `potential_fall`, `demo`) emitting official `CSI_DATA` lines. Noise, motion strength, event duration and packet rate are adjustable, and everything is marked synthetic.
- **Other code**: offline replay, CSV export, `backend/ml/train_rf.py`, the CLI `evaluate` command and `monitor --simulate`.
- **Server and UI**: the new simulation, alerts, events, export and heuristic-settings routes, the Simulation tab, the Alerts panel and the Export card.
- **Makefile**: new targets `simulate`, `dashboard-sim`, `evaluate` and `train-rf`.
- **README**: fully rewritten, keeping the disclaimer, the not-verified hardware/firmware statement, the Flask-instead-of-Streamlit reason, the no-auth note and a Verification status section.

**Deviations**
- The optional RF prediction in the dashboard was not built, since sklearn isn't in `.venv`.
- One old dashboard test expected `{kind: 'simulation'}` to be rejected. Simulation is now valid, so I replaced that case with invalid-parameter simulation requests.

Not verified: browser rendering, firmware compile, real hardware, and the heuristic on real CSI.
